title: Biliary tree anatomy
claims: Bile flows: hepatic ducts → common hepatic duct → (cystic duct to gallbladder) → common bile duct → ampulla of Vater (sphincter of Oddi) → duodenum.
Calot triangle is bounded by the cystic duct, common hepatic duct and inferior liver edge, and contains the cystic artery. It is a key landmark in cholecystectomy.
Cholelithiasis is often silent; biliary colic follows fatty meals (RUQ pain, 30 min to hours).
If a stone impacts the cystic duct and inflammation follows: acute cholecystitis (fever, Murphy sign, ↑WBC).
If infected, cholangitis shows Charcot triad (fever, jaundice, RUQ pain); add shock and confusion for Reynold pentad.
Cholangitis management: broad-spectrum antibiotics and urgent biliary decompression (ERCP).
A stone at the ampulla of Vater blocks the pancreatic duct and bile duct, causing gallstone pancreatitis (the most common cause with alcohol).
Gallstone pancreatitis presents with epigastric pain radiating to the back and ↑lipase, often with ↑ALT.
Mirizzi syndrome: a stone in the Hartmann pouch/cystic duct compresses the common hepatic duct, giving obstructive jaundice with a gallbladder source; diagnosed on imaging/ERCP.
Courvoisier sign: painless jaundice plus a palpable, non-tender gallbladder suggests malignant obstruction (e.g. pancreatic head cancer), not stones.
In Courvoisier sign the mass blocks the distal common bile duct, which dilates, as does the gallbladder.
